relationship noun

between people

also relations, close relationship, ties (between people), bond, be close to, be in a relationship

classical

Cic. Fam. 13.27.2: summā necessitūdine et summā conjūnctiōne adductus
Cic. Sest. 39: sunt mihi cum illō omnēs amīcitiae necessitūdinēs (Lewis & Short)

necessitūdō, necessitūdinis f.

noun, third declension

a close tie, a relationship (of family, friendship or duty)

Lewis & Short: “a close connection, in which one person stands to another as relative or friend”. Gellius (13.3.1) reports the grammarians’ distinction: necessitās is compulsion, necessitūdō a bond. A relationship “exists between” people: intercēdit, as in multaque et magna inter nōs officia paria et mūtua intercēdunt (Cic. Fam. 13.65.1).

Other words

  • familiāritās, familiāritātis f. — a close friendship, intimacy

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.65.1: mihi summa familiāritās cōnsuētūdōque est

  • cōnsuētūdō, cōnsuētūdinis f. — companionship, close acquaintance; (in comedy) a love affair

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.16.11: multā et jūcundā cōnsuētūdine conjūnctī inter nōs sumus; Ter. Hec. 404

    Also, and more often, a habit or custom.

  • conjūnctiō, conjūnctiōnis f. — a connection, a relationship (of kinship or friendship)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.10.4: in omnibus novīs conjūnctiōnibus

Examples

  • et hercule multā et jūcundā cōnsuētūdine conjūnctī inter nōs sumus

    and, I tell you, we are joined by a close and pleasant relationshipCic. Att. 1.16.11

  • in omnibus novīs conjūnctiōnibus interest quālis prīmus aditus sit

    in every new relationship a great deal depends on how the first approach is madeCic. Fam. 13.10.4

  • etsī amor mē graviter cōnsuētūdōque ejus tenet

    though love and my relationship with her still hold me fastTer. Hec. 404

See also friend, relative, love, depend.
